draft.title: Connection to Country
card: Country is the word many First Nations Australians use for the land, waters and sky that their family group belongs to. It includes the people, plants, animals and stories of that place.
A person's connection to Country comes through family, culture and history. It is passed down through kin, language, ceremony and stories.
Many First Nations people were dispossessed, which means their land was taken from them. Many were also relocated, which means they were moved away from Country to other places.
Connection to Country can continue across distance and time. It shapes a person's identity and their sense of belonging, so it also shapes how they see a place.
draft.remember: Country links people to place through family, culture and history, and it shapes identity and belonging.

a.q: Which of these best describes what Country means to many First Nations Australians?
opts: Land, waters and sky that a family group belongs to
A region of land that is owned by one person
A rural town that is far from services
The nation of Australia as a whole
a.why: Country includes the land, waters, sky, people and stories of a place that a family group belongs to. It is not only a piece of land or a type of settlement, because the connection is about belonging and culture.
a.clue: Think of belonging, not of ownership or distance.

b.q: Aunty Rose was moved as a child from her family's Country to a town far away. Now she lives in a city. What does the card suggest about her connection to Country?
opts: It can continue through family, stories and culture
It ended when she moved away from her Country
It now belongs to the city where she lives
It only exists while a person lives on that land
b.why: Connection comes through family, culture and history, and these can be passed on across distance and time. Relocation is part of the history, but it does not end the connection. It can shape Aunty Rose's identity and sense of belonging.
b.clue: Where does the connection come from, apart from living on the land?

a.best: Land, waters and sky that a family group belongs to

b.best: It can continue through family, stories and culture

problems.detail: The clue 'Think of belonging, not of ownership or distance' rules out two distractors and echoes 'belongs to' in the right option, so a student can match the word without knowing the idea.
The right option is the only one with the qualifier 'can'; the distractors are all absolute ('only exists', 'ended', 'now belongs'). A student could pick it on that pattern alone.

b.q: Aunty Rose was moved as a child from her family's Country to a town far away. Now she lives in a city. What can keep her connected to her Country?
opts: Family, language, ceremony and stories
Owning a block of land in the city
Being close to city shops and hospitals
Joining a sports club in her new suburb
b.why: Connection to Country is passed down through kin, language, ceremony and stories, so it can continue even after relocation. Owning city land is about property in a different place, not a link to her family's Country.
b.clue: How is connection to Country passed down?
